chunks.arabic_text: ٤ - الْقَاسِمُ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينَ، أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ، سَكَنَ قُمٌ. حَدِيثَهُ نَعْرِفُهُ، وَنُنْكِرُهُ. ذَكَرَ الْقُمِّيُّونَ: أَنَّ فِي مَذْهَبِهِ ارْتِفَاعًا. وَالْأَغْلَبُ عَلَيْهِ الْخَيْرُ.

translations.en: 4 – Al-Qāsim ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, Abū Muḥammad. Settled in Qum. We recognize his ḥadīth and we deny them. The Qummis mentioned: indeed in his madhhab there is irtifāʿ. Most of what is upon him is good.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Ḍuʿafāʾ* highlights the nuanced evaluation of Al-Qāsim ibn Yaqṭīn, a key figure in the early Qum scholarly circle. The mention of 'irtifāʿ' (elevation) suggests a potential rise in his status or a specific doctrinal elevation within his school of thought, which the Qummis viewed positively despite the ambiguity in his narrations. This reflects the Shia tradition of balancing strict scrutiny of individual narrators with an appreciation for their overall contribution to the community's religious life.
en.seo_question: Who is Al-Qāsim ibn Yaqṭīn and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.يَقْطِينَ: Yaqṭīn (a common Shia narrator name, often associated with the Banu Yaqṭin family)
key_terms.قُمٌ: Qum (a major center of Shia scholarship and hadith transmission)
key_terms.مَذْهَبِهِ: madhhab (here referring to his school of thought or method of transmitting hadith, not necessarily a legal school)
key_terms.ارْتِفَاعًا: irtifāʿ (elevation, rising, or increase, often used in biographical evaluations to denote rising status or knowledge)
